newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bonds weaker, crown softer in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bonds weaker, crown softer in light trade.

text.p: Swedish bond yields rose on Thursday morning while shorter maturities dropped one point with the focus on the U.S..
"There isn't much activity in the market and small volumes easily push the yields," one dealer said.
The market is focusing on U.S. statistics due later on Thursday including the U.S. trade balance for October, weekly unemployment figures and the Philadelphia Fed survey on the economic outlook.
Sweden's central bank held a board meeting but, as expected, no rate changes were announced.
However, there was some speculation that the German Bundesbank would lower its rates at a meeting on Thursday.
"There is some speculation but most people expect the Bundesbank to keep rates unchanged," one dealer said.
The six-month T-bill rates dropped one basis point to 3.88 percent and the ten-year bond yield rose by three basis points to 6.82 percent.
The crown softened in calm trade to 4.4060 crowns to the mark compared with 4.4030 late on Wednesday.
